card: Adds a GitHub Actions CI workflow that builds release packages using Guix for Linux, macOS, and Windows, then runs unit and functional tests on the resulting binaries using native runners. Currently, Guix release binaries and codesigning environments are not continuously built or tested in CI, leaving packaging breakages, missing codesign dependencies, and compiler toolchain quirks undiscovered until manual release engineering. Testing these binaries continuously also provides necessary infrastructure for introducing fully static Linux builds in #25573.
changed_since_previous: No structural changes to the PR's functionality; minor CI workflow runner and dependency adjustments from rebasing.
evidence: Description: "Currently there is limited continuous testing of our exact release binaries... in the event that we start shipping some fully-static Linux builds (x64 and aarch64) as per current revision of #25573, our entire custom-built static glibc and compiler toolchain would be relatively untested by current CI jobs, and that would also be tested here."

Commit df5787913b: "The regular Guix builds do not evaluate the codesign manifest, so missing imports and broken signing dependencies can go unnoticed until signing. Realize each signing target's environment before its main build to catch these failures without requiring signatures or signing keys."
problem: Bitcoin Core does not continuously build or test its actual Guix release packages or codesign environments in CI. Packaging errors, missing codesigning dependencies, and toolchain-specific runtime bugs can go unnoticed until release engineering, and major toolchain additions like fully static Linux binaries have no continuous test coverage.

risk.why: Mistakes could break CI jobs or increase runner flakiness, but only affect CI workflows and Guix wrapper scripts without altering production node logic.

scope_notes: Adds a major GitHub Actions workflow involving Docker-based Guix container builds, cross-runner artifact sharing, and native execution on Linux, macOS, and Windows runners.
summary: Adds a GitHub Actions CI workflow that produces release packages using Guix for Linux (x86_64), macOS (arm64), and Windows (x86_64), and executes unit and functional tests on the resulting binaries across native runners. It evaluates the Guix codesign manifest ahead of time to verify signing environments, preserves test configuration files from the build tree, and exports Guix time-machine metadata for container caching.
